claim: Syzygy now best-effort signs the exact retained full adversarial-review archive and each exact immutable accept/reject decision after the shared mutation commits, through both product and MCP paths. Verification re-resolves the retained event hash and stored participant, while signing failure remains explicit and never rolls back research history.
commands: node ../scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- cmd.exe /d /s /c "npm exec vitest -- run src/extensions/adversarialHistory.test.ts src/workspace/projectResearchEventAttestation.test.ts src/workspace/AdversarialReviewWorkspace.ui.test.tsx"
proved: Archive attribution hashes the exact strict archive envelope, including its content-addressed record hash, full question, frozen sources, results, baselines, and provenance; changed stored content no longer verifies.
Decision attribution hashes the exact run/archive identity, decision ID, prior decision ID, decision, stored participant/display name, notes, and timestamp; changed notes or lineage no longer verify.
Publication requires the self-reported stored participant to match an unconflicted registered installation key. Correctly signed cross-author archive and decision claims are rejected.

Product and MCP save/decide paths commit immutable shared history before best-effort signing, expose signed-device or bounded unsigned attribution, and return the post-attribution revision where applicable.
Headless inspection returns bounded event/key/participant/hash metadata without archive bodies, decision notes, proof bodies, signatures, public keys, or display names.
notProved: That a self-issued installation key authenticates a person or organization, establishes truth or consensus, prevents Sybil identities, or represents legal or organizational consent.
Append-only survival against a malicious Yjs writer, trusted time, identity-key rotation/recovery, live paid-provider quality, or physical packaged two-install interaction.
Signed production adoption for suggestion, heuristic, or scenario-rerun events; those three named research-event domains remain contract-only.
